coverage_notes: Two cross-cutting concept families (label/state and ticket-topic grammar) have source-level checks. A separate index accounts for all 275 inherited duplication-category findings in the 29 existing raw units; indexing is not semantic reconciliation. This is not a complete concept sweep of the 32 planned review boundaries. Existing defect IDs are retained; no new defect or LOC-saving count is inferred from source similarities.

findings.title: Agent label interpretation has several incompatible contracts
findings.description: Seeded lifecycle labels, agent write permissions, current issue tag selection and TUI terminal-tag filtering all interpret related strings but serve different contracts. State.issue_tag chooses the first literal agent: label, including markers, while Summaries filters only three fixed terminal tags. A custom configured prefix or marker order can therefore alter synthetic helper output. The isolated probe does not establish production incidence. This overlaps agent-runtime-23 and agent-backends-cc-38; preserve those source IDs and do not count this as an additional defect.
findings.recommendation: Represent canonical tracker disposition, marker labels, agent write authority and TUI work state separately. Share typed parsing and vocabulary where the contracts align; keep a positive write-permission policy and source provenance.

findings.title: Ticket event topic construction and parsing lack one grammar owner
findings.description: PR poll and webhook adapters construct the same topic suffixes, while wake projection and orchestrator topics parse ticket fields and suffixes through separate regex/split/branch paths. The concept is a typed ticket-topic grammar, not a single unqualified string helper: preserve ticket identifier domain, event source and suffix-specific payload rules. This overlaps three inherited topic findings and name draft 03; retain their IDs and validate the claimed 106 producers/11+ parsers separately before using those counts.
findings.recommendation: Give event topics an owner for typed construction and parsing, with source adapters retaining their event admission and replay semantics.
